title: The Last Wolf Anew
premise: When the crown of Vessany declares a hunt for the gifted, Paloma Marchetti flees the magic-dead valley that raised her, carrying her dead mentor's grimoire and a rumor: a door out of a country that was erased from maps a century ago still opens for those who can name it. Hunted by a wolf-blooded captain, Aldric, who is himself hiding a suppressed gift, Paloma discovers the erased nation of Vessany was destroyed by its own king to bury the door—and that opening it will unmake the valley that shielded everyone she loves. Across thirteen turns of the moon, she and Aldric fall in love while piecing together the door's true name, until Paloma must choose: pass through to freedom alone, or spend her gift sealing the door forever, binding herself to a homeland that no longer exists but choosing, at last, who she is.
about_author: Isandro Marchetti is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade drawing borders for governments before turning to stories about the places borders erase. They write from a house at the edge of a valley, where they insist the fog reads over their shoulder.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In the magic-dead valley, Paloma hides her small gift by never using it, tending her dying mentor Maren's herb garden. When Maren dies whispering about 'the door and the thirteenth turn,' Paloma burns the warning and keeps the grimoire. Beat: grief and the first crack in her carefully ordinary life.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Well
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A crown crier reads the Edict of the Hunt: all gifted persons must register or be taken. A neighbor's child, caught lighting candles with a thought, is dragged away. Paloma packs in the night. Beat: fear curdling into resolve; the valley's safety revealed as an illusion.

chapters.title: What Maren Never Taught
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. On the road, Paloma opens the grimoire and finds pages written to her by name, including a map of Vessany with a door marked where no country exists. She attempts her first deliberate spell and it answers too eagerly. Beat: wonder shadowed by the sense of being watched by her mentor's ghost.

chapters.title: The Captain with Winter Eyes
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Captain Aldric Vane leads the hunt, secretly concealing his own wolf-blood gift behind iron charms. He interrogates a village and lets a gifted boy slip away, hating himself. Beat: establish the antagonist who is a prisoner of his own duty.

chapters.title: Crossing the Old March
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma crosses into Vessany's former territory, where the land is wrong—roads that loop, villages with no names. She meets Tamsin, a smuggler who trades in erased memories, and buys passage with a lock of her hair. Beat: the world opens; first taste of the uncanny.

chapters.title: Hounds of the Edict
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The hunt corners Paloma at a river ford. Aldric captures her but, recognizing a fellow hider, falsifies his report and becomes her reluctant escort under pretext of interrogation. Beat: the central alliance forms on a lie both of them see through.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons, Counting
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Tamsin explains the legend: the door out of Vessany opens only during the thirteenth lunar turn, once a century. Paloma counts the nights—eleven remain. She practices magic with Aldric watching, and for the first time doesn't flinch from her gift. Beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: The City with No Name
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating. They reach the ruined capital, where the erased nation's ghosts replay a single night: the king sealing the door with a sacrifice. Paloma learns the door demands a name freely given, and that her mentor Maren was born here. Beat: awe and dread; the stakes become personal history.

chapters.title: Iron Charms
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Aldric's charms crack; his wolf-sense surges during a checkpoint inspection, nearly exposing them both. Paloma covers for him, and he confesses what he is. Beat: vulnerability exchanged for trust; the hunter becomes the hunted.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Price
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Tamsin reveals she sold the door's location to the crown years ago and offers to buy it back—for Paloma's memories of the valley. Paloma refuses and they part as enemies of a sort. Beat: the price of survival made literal; a friendship lost.

chapters.title: Moonturn Nine
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The hunt's true commander, Inquisitor Serane, arrives, suspicious of Aldric's empty reports. A night skirmish in the ruins forces Paloma to use her gift publicly to save villagers. Beat: the mask comes off; now she is the hunt's declared quarry.

chapters.title: What the Valley Was For
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In the grimoire's final pages, Paloma learns the truth: the magic-dead valley was built as a cage around the door's key—her own bloodline. Maren didn't hide her; she guarded her. Beat: identity shattered; her whole life reinterpreted as a sentence.

chapters.title: The Wolf and the Witch
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Wounded protecting Paloma, Aldric finally lets his gift loose, and they shelter in a chapel where they speak honestly for the first time—about duty, fear, and what freedom would even mean. Beat: the love confessed quietly, between bandages and candlelight.

chapters.title: Serane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. The Inquisitor offers Aldric pardon and purpose if he delivers the witch; she reveals she knows the door is the crown's true target—the king wants to leave the country he's bankrupting. Beat: raise the stakes—the hunt is a cover for the crown's own escape.

chapters.title: Moonturn Eleven
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Two turns remain. Paloma and Aldric reach the door's antechamber beneath the ruins and find it already guarded by crown soldiers. Tamsin reappears, having decided memories are a fair price for redemption, and buys them a distraction with her own past. Beat: sacrifice as atonement; the plan crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Name in the Grimoire
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma deciphers the door's true name and learns the terrible symmetry: it opens only if someone with valley blood gives their name to it—permanently. Whoever opens it cannot pass through. Beat: the choice takes shape; love against duty made concrete.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn Rising
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The moon begins its thirteenth turn. Serane storms the ruins with the hunt; Aldric holds the stairway alone in wolf-form while Paloma descends. Beat: climax begins—everything converging on one door in one night.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Vessany
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the door, the king himself arrives, demanding passage. Paloma speaks the name and the door opens—but she understands she can never walk through it. Serane falls in the collapse of the crown's ambitions; Aldric reaches her as the light spills out. Beat: climax—the door opens and the cost is named.

chapters.title: What Paloma Gave
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Instead of fleeing, Paloma gives the door not her escape but her name as its keeper, sealing it and unmaking the crown's escape while sparing the valley. The magic-dead valley dissolves into ordinary, giftless land—free, not caged. Beat: the price paid; survival redefined as choosing your bonds.

chapters.title: Ash and Aftermath
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The hunt dissolves; Aldric breaks his iron charms for good and refuses a new commission. He finds Paloma alive but nameless in the old sense—no longer Marchetti, no longer anyone's apprentice or quarry. Beat: grief and tenderness; two people unmade by duty finding each other.

chapters.title: A Country of Two
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Paloma and Aldric return to the valley, which remembers nothing and needs no guarding. They rebuild Maren's garden; Paloma teaches a gifted child to hold her gift gently. Beat: resolution—love chosen freely, identity built rather than inherited.

chapters.title: The Last Wolf Anew
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, years later. On the night of the thirteenth turn's anniversary, the door stirs once and offers her a final passage. She touches the stone, says her own new name aloud, and walks home instead. Beat: quiet coda—freedom is not the door out, but the life you build on this side of it.
